results.title: Troubleshooting Playback Download Errors
results.summary: Covers four named download error messages in Playback (Error Authorizing, Audio Files Missing, Insufficient Storage, generic Download Error) plus a catch-all. MultiTracks says download errors are rare and asks users who see the same error repeatedly to report it through the website chat. The article does not name a platform; it refers only to 'the device' and 'the Playback app'. Each step belongs to its named-error section. The remove/re-add and alternate-key quick fixes are documented under generic Download Error; that section does not establish them as Audio Files Missing recovery.

steps.text: 'Error Authorizing': the download failed a security check (your network may be blocking Playback from verifying the device). Follow the separate article 'Playback Download Error (Download Unauthorized)'.
'Audio Files Missing': tap Try Again at least three times. On the third attempt Playback runs a different recovery routine automatically.

'Audio Files Missing' (if three attempts fail on a song you recently downloaded in past setlists): open the setlist menu, scroll to the bottom, and select 'Delete All Setlists from Device'. Last resort only: it removes all local downloads and every current setlist must be downloaded again.
steps.caution: This removes the song from the device and re-downloads it, so only do it when you have time before you play.

steps.text: 'Insufficient Storage': remove past setlists with 'Delete all setlists from device' at the bottom of the setlist menu. If the error persists, check the device's storage; it may be too full. A typical song is roughly 40 MB to 1 GB, so a full setlist can be several GB.
steps.caution: This removes the song from the device and re-downloads it, so only do it when you have time before you play.

steps.text: 'Download Error' (generic): tap Try Again at least two times. If it continues and you are short on time, use Contact Support in the About tab of Playback Settings, then try the quick fixes.

'Download Error' (generic section, after retries and contacting support) - Quick fix 1 - remove and re-add the song: tap Edit, tap the red minus icon on the song, tap '+ Add Song', find the song again, and load it.
steps.caution: This removes the song from the device and re-downloads it, so only do it when you have time before you play.

steps.text: 'Download Error' (generic section, after retries and contacting support) - Quick fix 2 - download in another key and transpose locally: before loading, change the song's key in song settings to a key close to the one you need; after the download, open song settings in edit mode and change the key back.

'Download Error' (generic section, after retries and contacting support) - Quick fix 3 - clear local data (last resort): contact support first from the About tab, then open the setlist menu (top-right) and select 'Delete All Setlists from Device' at the bottom. All setlists must be redownloaded afterward.
steps.caution: This removes the song from the device and re-downloads it, so only do it when you have time before you play.

steps.text: Any other error: contact MultiTracks.com through the website messenger or 'Contact Support' in the About tab of the Playback app.

results.title: How To | Track & Bus Routing in Playback
results.summary: Playback has dedicated Click and Guide buses by default. Bus routing and MultiOuts require a Playback Premium subscription. Playback groups 150+ instruments into 16 buses plus a dedicated SMPTE bus; each bus can go to any available output on the selected audio device, mono or stereo. The Pad bus cannot be re-routed. Track routing is saved per device and applies globally to that track; it is not saved with setlists or named arrangements. Separate buses assigned to the same output still share that hardware feed. For independent external control, use distinct available outputs matching the caller's connected desk channels; example output numbers are not universal assignments.

steps.text: Route tracks to buses: Settings > Tracks tab, assign each track to a bus (defaults are preset and can be overwritten).
Route buses to outputs: Settings > Buses tab, tap a bus row and choose an available output.
Route several buses at once: tap 'Assign Multiple Busses' in the bottom-right, select buses, assign one output.
Rename a bus: drag its row to the left to reveal Edit.
Greyed-out output: the SMPTE bus is probably using it. Disable SMPTE in the General tab or set the SMPTE bus to 'None'.

Alternative from the main interface: open the 'Busses' layer (bottom right next to the master fader, or cycle layers with the button beside it), tap Edit (top right) to enter Setlist/Song Map edit mode, tap a bus name and select the output.
Bus mixes are song-specific by default; disable Song Specific Buses in Settings for a global mix. Solo/mute on a bus affects all tracks routed to it.

results.title: Playback General Settings Overview
results.summary: Lists every setting in the General tab (three-line menu icon top-right > General). Audio-relevant items: Auto-Pan, Click Sound, Song Specific Buses (Premium), Audio Device (shows and sets which connected device Playback uses for all audio output), Power Saver, MIDI Out, and SMPTE Timecode. The page gives no detail on Audio Device choices and does not mention sample rate, Bluetooth, storage, or subscription display.

steps.text: Open settings: tap the three-line menu icon in the top-right corner of Playback and make sure the General tab is selected.
Audio Device: shows and sets which connected audio device Playback uses for all audio output.
Auto-Pan: routes click and guide to the left mono output and all tracks to the right mono output of the device's stereo output.
Song Specific Buses (Premium): on gives each song its own bus fader mix; off uses one global bus mix.
Power Saver: improves performance on older devices; disables fader VU meters and fader multi-touch and reduces waveform scrolling feedback.
MIDI Out: enabled by default; disable if unused to improve performance and battery life.
SMPTE Timecode: toggles SMPTE output and selects frame rate.
Fader Default Level at 80%: on presets faders to 80% for headroom; off loads tracks at 100%.

results.sectionPath: Playback User Guide > Building a Setlist > Adding A Song in Playback
results.text: To add a song in Playback, Tap “Add A Song” on the Setlist row to open the 'Add a Song' Menu. You'll have a number of options to navigate the song or product you'd like to add into Playback. Or simply use the top search to search through all songs.

results.sectionPath: Playback User Guide > Building a Setlist > Adding a song > Settings available when adding a song:
results.text:
After confirming the song is loading in with the desired settings, tap Add in the top right corner of the menu, and the song will begin downloading on your device.

Continuing adding additional songs to the setlist by repeating the steps as needed, and make sure to always Save to cloud when finished making any setlist changes. Saving your setlist to the cloud not only protects your changes but also synchronizes the setlist to all devices logged into your MultiTracks.com account, ensuring consistent access during rehearsals and performances.
